title: Prophylaxis: ask what he wants to play
outcomes: Explains prophylaxis as asking what the opponent wants to play, and says it is not passivity
Names the opponent's real freeing move and the move that prevents it
Leaves the move alone when the opponent has nothing real to prevent

steps.text:
**Prophylaxis** means asking, before you move: what does my opponent want to play? If that move would free his position or hurt yours, prevent it.
It is not passivity: a quiet move can be the most useful move on the board. Use it when his move is real and your own plan can wait.

steps.caption: White to move. Black's pawn on c6 could advance to c5.

line.say: b4: the pawn now attacks c5.
Black doubles on the c-file with the rook.

claims.statement: A black pawn stands on c6.
After b4 one White pawn attacks c5.
At depth 16 the engine puts Bxb6 and b4 within 40 centipawns of each other.
Nf3 is at least 80 centipawns worse than the best move.

steps.text:
Prophylaxis pays when his freeing move is real and one useful move stops it. It wastes a tempo when he cannot carry the move out, or when you have something faster.
**Rule of thumb:** find his best move first (imagine you pass). If passing would cost you nothing, carry on with your own plan.

steps.title: Prevent, or carry on?
steps.prompt: Predict which move is best in each position. In the second, Black has no d-pawn. The third is a different case.
Before your next move in a game, write down what your opponent wants to play. Did you do that today? What did you find?
